relatedSourceMoves.claimSummary: Religion is an inherited explanatory form from humanity's scientific infancy, not a true account of the world.
relatedSourceMoves.reasonSummary: Early humans lacked knowledge of astronomy, germs, microorganisms, geology, and natural causes, so fearful minds supplied intentional or conspiratorial forms that later became fixed traditions.

inferenceSummary.premise: Religious explanations arose when key natural mechanisms were unknown and are displaced as those mechanisms become understood.
inferenceSummary.inference: An explanation traceable to systematic ignorance and retained after natural explanations arrive has no earned truth advantage.
inferenceSummary.conclusion: Religion's account of reality should not be accepted as true merely because it is ancient or culturally persistent.

relatedSourceMoves.claimSummary: A scientist's private faith can coexist with achievement without being supported by the science, whereas modern biology coheres with God's extreme unlikelihood.
relatedSourceMoves.reasonSummary: Hitchens cites Newton, Priestley, and Hoyle as brilliant people who also held discarded beliefs, distinguishing personal conviction from conclusions warranted by their disciplines.
